intent.raw_query: Swiss Alps ski holiday family, $7000, 7 days, February

experiences.name: Zermatt Ski Safari
experiences.description: Explore the world-renowned ski slopes of Zermatt with access to over 360km of pistes across Switzerland and Italy. Ski beneath the iconic Matterhorn with breathtaking panoramic views. Suitable for intermediate to advanced skiers with varied terrain including groomed runs and off-piste adventures.

experiences.name: Jungfrau Region Snowshoeing & Winter Hiking
experiences.description: Guided snowshoeing tour through the stunning Jungfrau region, trekking through pristine alpine landscapes, frozen lakes, and snow-covered forests. Visit the Aletsch Glacier viewpoint, the largest glacier in the Alps, and enjoy a traditional Swiss fondue lunch at a mountain hut along the trail.

experiences.name: St. Moritz Ice Skating & Bobsled Experience
experiences.description: Skate on the legendary frozen Lake St. Moritz and then experience the thrill of riding the historic Olympia Bob Run, one of the world's oldest natural ice bobsled tracks dating back to 1904. A unique adrenaline-pumping winter activity combining culture and sport in the glamorous St. Moritz setting.

experiences.name: Glacier 3000 Suspension Bridge & Peak Walk
experiences.description: Take the cable car up to Glacier 3000 and walk across the Peak Walk by Tissot, the world's first suspension bridge connecting two mountain peaks at 3,000 meters altitude. Enjoy 360-degree views of 24 Alpine peaks including Mont Blanc and the Matterhorn, and optionally try the glacier ski area or snow bus ride.

experiences.name: Traditional Swiss Alpine Cuisine & Cheese Cellar Tour
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in authentic Swiss mountain culture with a guided visit to a traditional alpine cheese cellar in the Appenzell region, learning how Gruyère and Raclette are crafted. Follow with a hands-on fondue and raclette cooking class paired with local Swiss wines and schnapps in a cozy chalet setting.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich or Milan Malpensa airport, take a regional train or bus toward Poschiavo via the Bernina Express route. Check in to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. Settle in, unpack, and get a good night's rest to prepare for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In transit
meals.lunch: N/A - In transit
meals.dinner: Grab a quick and affordable bite at the airport or train station (sandwiches, pretzels, or a kebab wrap for ~CHF 8-12). Alternatively, pick up snacks at a Migros or Coop convenience store en route.

day_by_day.notes: The Bernina Express route from Chur to Tirano passes through Poschiavo — a scenic and budget-friendly way to arrive. Book train tickets in advance via SBB.ch for the best fares. The B&B may have a late check-in arrangement; confirm with the host beforehand. Keep CHF cash on hand as smaller establishments in Poschiavo may not accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: After a hearty B&B breakfast, take a short walk to explore the charming village of Poschiavo. Stroll through the historic Piazza Comunale, admire the Spanish-style architecture unique to this Graubünden valley, and visit the local market if open. The crisp mountain air and snow-dusted rooftops make for a beautiful introduction to the Swiss Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby Lago di Poschiavo (Lake Poschiavo), which may be partially frozen in February — a stunning winter spectacle. Walk along the lakeside path (~3 km loop) and take in panoramic views of the surrounding snow-capped peaks. This is a free activity and perfect for photography and acclimatization.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the village center and explore the local shops. Visit the Coop or local grocery store to stock up on budget-friendly snacks, fruit, and drinks for the week. Relax at the B&B and plan the upcoming ski days.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — enjoy local bread, cheese, cold cuts, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch with items from the local Coop supermarket — bread, cheese, salami, and fruit for ~CHF 8-10.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Albrici in Poschiavo — a local favorite offering traditional Graubünden cuisine. Try the pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta) or polenta dishes for ~CHF 18-25. Budget-friendly by Swiss standards.

day_by_day.notes: Poschiavo sits at about 1,014 m elevation. Take it easy today to acclimatize before hitting the slopes. The lake walk is flat and accessible. Wear warm, waterproof layers as February temperatures can drop to -5°C to -10°C at night.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Bernina Express train (or PostBus) from Poschiavo up to Pontresina or St. Moritz — both accessible within 30-45 minutes. Head to the Diavolezza ski area, one of the most spectacular and accessible ski resorts in the Engadin valley. Purchase a day ski pass (look for early-bird or online discounts; ~CHF 60-70 for a day pass). Spend the morning on beginner to intermediate runs with breathtaking glacier views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing at Diavolezza. The resort offers runs for all levels, including the famous Diavolezza glacier descent. Take a break at the mountain restaurant — order a simple soup or rösti to keep costs down (~CHF 12-16). Enjoy the stunning views of Piz Palü and Piz Bernina from the top station at 2,978 m.
day_by_day.evening: Return by train to Poschiavo. Warm up with a hot shower and rest tired muscles. Consider a self-cooked meal at the B&B if kitchen facilities are available.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B.
meals.lunch: Mountain hut lunch at Diavolezza — a bowl of goulash soup and bread for ~CHF 12-15. Bring a thermos of tea or hot chocolate from the B&B to save on drinks.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner using groceries from Coop — pasta with tomato sauce, canned vegetables, and local cheese for ~CHF 6-8 per person. Or try Osteria Sonne in Poschiavo for a budget pasta dish (~CHF 16-20).

day_by_day.notes: Rent ski equipment in Poschiavo or at the resort base — renting locally may be cheaper. Check SBB.ch for train schedules; the Bernina line runs regularly. Book ski passes online in advance at diavolezza.ch for potential discounts. Bring sunscreen — UV rays are intense at high altitude even in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Take the PostBus or train toward Livigno (just across the Italian border, ~45 min from Poschiavo). Livigno is a duty-free ski resort with significantly cheaper ski passes, equipment rentals, and food compared to Swiss resorts. Purchase a day ski pass (~€35-45) and hit the slopes early. The resort has 115 km of pistes suitable for all levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Livigno's varied terrain — try the Carosello 3000 area for wide, open intermediate runs or the Mottolino area for more challenging descents. The duty-free status means cheaper après-ski snacks and drinks. Take a mid-afternoon break and browse the duty-free shops for affordable Swiss chocolate and snacks to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo via PostBus. Enjoy a relaxed evening at the B&B. If energy allows, take a short evening stroll through Poschiavo's illuminated historic center.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a Livigno mountain restaurant — pizza or pasta for ~€10-14, significantly cheaper than Swiss resorts. Take advantage of the duty-free pricing on beverages.
meals.dinner: Pick up duty-free Italian wine or snacks in Livigno for a cozy self-catered dinner back at the B&B (~€8-10). Alternatively, dine at a local Poschiavo trattoria for ~CHF 15-20.

day_by_day.notes: Livigno is technically in Italy but easily accessible from Poschiavo. Bring your passport as you cross an international border. The duty-free status makes Livigno one of the most budget-friendly ski destinations in the Alps. Check PostBus schedules at postauto.ch — the route may require a change at Le Prese or Tirano.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day from skiing — give your legs a break. After breakfast, take the Bernina Express train up to the Ospizio Bernina station (2,253 m) — the highest point on the Bernina railway line and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The journey itself is a spectacular winter experience with viaducts, frozen lakes, and glacier views. Disembark and explore the area around Lago Bianco (White Lake), which is frozen solid in February.
day_by_day.afternoon: Try snowshoeing or winter hiking around the Bernina Pass area. Snowshoe rentals are available in Pontresina (~CHF 15-20/day). The flat terrain around Lago Bianco is perfect for beginners. Alternatively, take the train to Pontresina and explore the village on foot, visiting the free Romanesque murals in the Santa Maria Chapel.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by train. Treat yourself to a fondue or raclette dinner — a quintessential Swiss Alps experience. Look for a local restaurant offering a set fondue menu for ~CHF 22-28 per person.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B.
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from the B&B or buy sandwiches at the Ospizio Bernina station café (~CHF 8-12). Enjoy eating outdoors with panoramic Alpine views.
meals.dinner: Fondue dinner at a local Poschiavo restaurant — Ristorante Albrici or Hotel Croce Federale often offer traditional fondue. Budget ~CHF 22-28 per person including a glass of local wine.

day_by_day.notes: The Bernina Express train pass is included if you have a Swiss Travel Pass — otherwise a single ticket from Poschiavo to Ospizio Bernina costs ~CHF 12-15 each way. Book in advance at sbb.ch. Dress in extra warm layers for the Bernina Pass — temperatures can reach -15°C with wind chill. The Lago Bianco area is flat and safe for casual winter walking.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the slopes for a final ski day. Head to Corvatsch or Corviglia near St. Moritz via the Bernina train. These are world-class ski areas with stunning Engadin valley views. Purchase a half-day pass (available from noon, ~CHF 40-50) or look for a full-day pass with a student/youth discount if applicable. Spend the morning on the train enjoying the scenery and arrive at the resort by mid-morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ski the Corviglia area above St. Moritz — excellent intermediate runs with views over the frozen St. Moritz Lake. Take a break to walk through St. Moritz village (window shopping is free!) and admire the glamorous resort town. Visit the free Segantini Museum exterior or the frozen lake where polo and cricket matches are sometimes held in February.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo for a celebratory final dinner. Splurge slightly on a sit-down meal at a local restaurant to celebrate the trip.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B.
meals.lunch: Budget mountain lunch — bring a packed sandwich and thermos from the B&B, or grab a bratwurst from a mountain kiosk (~CHF 8-10).
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at Ristorante Albrici or Hotel Croce Federale in Poschiavo — try the local specialty of pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta with cheese and vegetables) or a hearty Graubünden meat platter. Budget ~CHF 25-35 per person with a local beer or wine.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is the busiest day on Swiss ski slopes — arrive early to avoid lift queues. St. Moritz is expensive for dining and shopping, so stick to the slopes and avoid the luxury boutiques. The train back to Poschiavo runs regularly — check the last departure time to avoid being stranded. Consider buying a souvenir at the Coop or local shop rather than St. Moritz boutiques.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Poschiavo. After a leisurely B&B breakfast, take a last walk through the village. Visit the local Sunday market if available, or simply stroll through the historic Borgo district one more time. Pack your bags and check out of the B&B. Take a few final photos of the snow-covered Poschiavo valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Poschiavo via the Bernina Express toward Chur or Tirano (depending on your return flight route). The train journey is a final scenic treat — the Bernina line crosses 196 bridges and passes through 55 tunnels, offering incredible Alpine panoramas. If time allows before your departure, stop in Chur (Switzerland's oldest city) for a quick walk through the medieval old town.
day_by_day.evening: Travel to your departure airport (Zurich or Milan Malpensa). Allow ample time for check-in and security. Reflect on an incredible week of skiing, mountain scenery, and Swiss Alpine culture.

meals.breakfast: Final B&B breakfast — enjoy it fully as it's included.
meals.lunch: Grab a budget meal at Chur train station or a Migros/Coop takeaway counter (~CHF 8-12). Try a Swiss-style sandwich or warm soup.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or a final meal near the airport — budget ~CHF 15-20 at an airport Coop or casual restaurant. Alternatively, use up any remaining Swiss Francs on airport snacks and duty-free Swiss chocolate.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time at the B&B is typically 10:00-11:00 AM — confirm with the host. The Bernina Express is a UNESCO World Heritage railway — even on departure day, the journey is a highlight. Book return train tickets in advance at sbb.ch. If flying from Milan Malpensa, the train to Tirano (Italy) connects to buses toward Milan. Keep CHF 10-15 in reserve for any unexpected transport costs or luggage storage.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Transfer from airport to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. Check in, settle into your room, and get a good night's rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Late arrival at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama (~23:30–00:00). If the B&B has a small snack or welcome tray available, enjoy it before bed. Otherwise, grab a light snack from any airport or station kiosk during transit.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the airport before departure
meals.lunch: On the flight or at a transit stop
meals.dinner: Light snack from airport/train station kiosk or vending machine at the B&B upon arrival — no formal dinner due to late arrival time

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is at 22:30. Factor in baggage claim (~30 min), ground transport to Poschiavo (~1.5–2 hrs depending on route via Zurich or Milan). Pre-arrange a taxi or private transfer in advance as public transport options are very limited after 22:00 to Poschiavo. Confirm late check-in with the B&B ahead of time.

day_by_day.morning: Slow start and recovery morning. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the B&B, then take a gentle orientation walk through the charming village of Poschiavo. Explore the historic town center, the Piazza Comunale, and the Spanish-style houses — a unique cultural gem in the Swiss Alps. Breathe in the crisp mountain air and get your bearings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take the scenic Bernina Express train to nearby St. Moritz (approx. 45–60 min). Begin the St. Moritz Ice Skating & Bobsled Experience — skate on the legendary frozen Lake St. Moritz, one of the most iconic winter settings in the world, then experience the thrill of riding the historic Olympia Bob Run, the world's only naturally iced bobsled track still in operation.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by early evening. Stroll along the village and wind down with a warm drink at a local café before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — enjoy local bread, cheese, cold cuts, and coffee included with your stay
meals.lunch: Casual lunch in St. Moritz — try Café Hauser or a mountain-side self-service restaurant for a mid-range meal (CHF 20–35). Try a warm Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup) and rösti.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ristorante Suisse in Poschiavo — a cozy local restaurant offering Italian-Swiss cuisine with pasta, risotto, and regional specialties. Budget CHF 30–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Bernina Express is a UNESCO World Heritage railway — even the short leg to St. Moritz is scenic and worth enjoying. Book the Bobsled Experience in advance as slots fill up quickly. Dress in warm, windproof layers for ice skating and the bobsled run. St. Moritz is upscale but budget-friendly options exist for food.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, head to Glacier 3000 for the Glacier 3000 Suspension Bridge & Peak Walk experience. Take the cable car from Col du Pillon (approx. 2.5 hrs drive from Poschiavo, or combine with a train to Gstaad area) up to 3,000 meters. Walk across the Peak Walk by Tissot — the world's first suspension bridge connecting two mountain peaks — and enjoy breathtaking panoramic views of 24 Alpine peaks including Mont Blanc, the Matterhorn, and the Eiger.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the glacier plateau — try the Snow Bus ride across the glacier, visit the glacier cave, or enjoy beginner-friendly ski runs directly on the glacier. The area offers accessible winter fun for all levels.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the return journey toward Poschiavo. Stop for dinner en route or back in the village.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the B&B — fuel up well before the longer travel day
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Botta 3000 Restaurant on the glacier — a mid-range mountain restaurant with stunning views. Try the daily soup, mountain pasta, or a Swiss cheese plate. Budget CHF 25–40.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Osteria Salis in Poschiavo — a beloved local osteria with Graubünden regional cuisine including pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta), venison, and local wines. Budget CHF 30–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Glacier 3000 is a longer day trip from Poschiavo (~2.5 hrs each way). Consider an early 07:30 departure to maximize time on the glacier. Alternatively, if driving is not preferred, take the train to Zweisimmen and connect to Col du Pillon by bus. Dress in full ski/mountain gear — temperatures at 3,000m can be -10°C to -20°C with wind chill. Cable car tickets: approx. CHF 49–59 per person.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day to Zermatt (approx. 3–3.5 hrs by train via Chur and Visp — a spectacular scenic journey). Depart after breakfast and arrive in Zermatt by late morning. Check your luggage at the Zermatt train station lockers. Begin the Zermatt Ski Safari — access over 360km of world-class pistes across Switzerland and Italy with the iconic Matterhorn as your backdrop. Morning skiing on the Rothorn or Sunnegga Paradise areas, ideal for intermediate skiers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Zermatt Ski Safari into the afternoon. Explore the Klein Matterhorn sector (highest ski area in the Alps at 3,883m) and enjoy runs down to Cervinia, Italy if conditions allow. Take in the unparalleled views of the Matterhorn from the slopes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by early evening train (or stay overnight in Zermatt if budget allows for one night — optional upgrade). Alternatively, enjoy dinner in Zermatt before the return journey.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the B&B before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch on the mountain at a mid-mountain restaurant in Zermatt — try Chez Vrony or Findlerhof for a mid-range mountain lunch with Matterhorn views. Budget CHF 30–50. Alternatively, pack a sandwich from a Zermatt bakery to save costs.
meals.dinner: If returning to Poschiavo: dinner at the B&B if they offer evening meals, or at Ristorante Suisse. If staying in Zermatt: try Restaurant Whymper-Stube for traditional Swiss fondue and raclette. Budget CHF 35–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Zermatt is a car-free village — all transport within is by electric vehicle or horse-drawn carriage. Ski rental is available in Zermatt (CHF 50–70/day for skis, boots, poles). A day ski pass for Zermatt costs approx. CHF 85–95. Book ski rentals in advance online for discounts. The Zermatt Ski Safari experience may include a guide — confirm booking details. Consider an early train departure (07:00–07:30) to maximize ski time.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the B&B after the big ski day. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast, then embark on the Traditional Swiss Alpine Cuisine & Cheese Cellar Tour. This immersive cultural experience takes you to a traditional alpine cheese cellar in the Graubünden region (accessible from Poschiavo), where you'll learn about centuries-old cheese-making traditions, taste aged alpine cheeses, and discover the art of Swiss mountain food culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the cheese tour, visit a local Poschiavo artisan shop or the Museo di Poschiavo to learn about the valley's unique Romansh and Italian-influenced heritage. Take a scenic afternoon snowshoe walk along the shores of Lago di Poschiavo — a beautiful frozen alpine lake just minutes from the village center.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Poschiavo. Browse the village, pick up local souvenirs (alpine cheese, local wines, Graubünden dried meats), and enjoy a quiet dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the B&B
meals.lunch: Lunch included or paired with the Cheese Cellar Tour — expect a rustic spread of local cheeses, cured meats, dark bread, and local wine or schnapps as part of the experience
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local Poschiavo restaurant — try a traditional Graubünden capuns (chard-wrapped dumplings) or maluns (potato dish). Budget CHF 25–40 per person. Try Café/Restaurant Croce Federale in Poschiavo.

day_by_day.notes: The Traditional Swiss Alpine Cuisine & Cheese Cellar Tour is a highlight for food lovers and provides a wonderful cultural contrast to the action-packed ski days. Confirm the exact pickup/meeting point for the tour from Poschiavo. Lago di Poschiavo snowshoe walk is free and requires only basic winter boots or snowshoes (rentable locally for CHF 10–15). A perfect, lower-intensity day to recharge mid-trip.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to the Jungfrau Region for the Jungfrau Region Snowshoeing & Winter Hiking guided tour (approx. 2.5–3 hrs by train via Chur and Interlaken). Depart early after breakfast. The guided snowshoeing tour takes you through pristine alpine landscapes of the Jungfrau region — one of Switzerland's most iconic mountain areas. Trek through snow-covered forests, open meadows, and dramatic glacier viewpoints with a certified mountain guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the snowshoeing tour into the afternoon. The guide will lead you to scenic viewpoints of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau peaks. After the tour, take the cogwheel train up to Kleine Scheidegg for panoramic views, or visit the Jungfraujoch — Top of Europe (optional add-on, CHF 145–175 — splurge option for a special experience).
day_by_day.evening: Return journey to Poschiavo by train. Arrive back in the village by 20:00–21:00. Light dinner or room service if available.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the B&B before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or quick stop at a mountain hut during the snowshoeing tour — the guide may recommend a traditional Bergrestaurant (mountain hut) for a warm soup and bread. Budget CHF 15–25.
meals.dinner: Simple, hearty dinner back in Poschiavo — try a local pizzeria or the B&B's recommended eatery. After a long active day, opt for comfort food like pasta, pizza, or a warm risotto. Budget CHF 20–35.

day_by_day.notes: The Jungfrau Region Snowshoeing tour is a guided experience — confirm meeting point (likely Grindelwald or Wengen). Snowshoes and poles are typically provided by the tour operator. Wear moisture-wicking base layers, insulating mid-layer, and a waterproof outer shell. Gaiters are recommended. The Jungfraujoch visit is optional but iconic — if budget allows, this is the day to splurge. Book Jungfraujoch tickets well in advance as they sell out, especially on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps. Enjoy a relaxed, extended breakfast at the B&B — savor the mountain views one last time. Take a final short walk through Poschiavo village or along the lake. Pack up and check out. If time allows before departure, visit the local Sunday market or pick up last-minute alpine souvenirs — local cheese, Bündnerfleisch (air-dried beef), Swiss chocolate, or a bottle of Valtelline wine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin your departure journey. Depending on your outbound flight, take the scenic Bernina Express or regional train toward Zurich, Milan, or your departure airport. The Bernina Express itself is a world-class farewell experience — a UNESCO Heritage railway winding through dramatic alpine scenery, viaducts, and glaciers.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Switzerland. Reflect on an incredible week of skiing, snowshoeing, glacier walks, cheese tastings, and alpine adventures in one of the world's most beautiful mountain destinations.

meals.breakfast: Final full breakfast at B&B Berninahaus Poschiavo Panorama — enjoy every last bite of Swiss bread, local cheese, and mountain coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at the train station or on the Bernina Express dining car — enjoy a sandwich, soup, or light meal while watching the alpine scenery roll by. Budget CHF 15–25.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Check out time at the B&B is typically 10:00–11:00 — confirm with the host. The Bernina Express to Tirano (Italy) or Chur runs several times daily and is one of the most scenic train rides in the world — a perfect farewell to the Alps. Book train tickets in advance via SBB (Swiss Federal Railways) app or website. If flying from Zurich, allow at least 3.5–4 hrs travel time from Poschiavo plus 2 hrs airport check-in time.

meals.dinner: In-room late-night snack platter arranged by the B&B — local cheeses, charcuterie, fresh bread, and herbal tea or a glass of Graubünden Pinot Noir

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private luxury transfer (Mercedes V-Class or similar) from the airport to Poschiavo. The drive from Zurich or Milan Malpensa to Poschiavo is approximately 2.5–3 hours. Confirm transfer timing with your concierge in advance. Pack light layers for the cold alpine arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the B&B with panoramic alpine views over the Bernina Pass. After breakfast, take a scenic private drive or the historic Bernina Express train toward St. Moritz (approximately 45 minutes from Poschiavo). Begin the St. Moritz Ice Skating & Bobsled Experience — skate on the legendary frozen Lake St. Moritz under crisp alpine skies, followed by an exhilarating ride on the historic Cresta Run or Olympic Bobsled track.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the glamorous village of St. Moritz at leisure. Browse luxury boutiques along Via Serlas, or visit the Segantini Museum for stunning alpine art. Enjoy a private guided snowshoe walk around the frozen lake perimeter with a local mountain guide for a more intimate alpine experience.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a top St. Moritz restaurant before returning to Poschiavo by private transfer. St. Moritz offers some of Switzerland's finest dining options for a memorable first full evening.

meals.breakfast: Full alpine breakfast at B&B Berninahaus — fresh pastries, local honey, Engadine nut tart, cold cuts, regional cheeses, and freshly brewed coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mathis Food Affairs (St. Moritz) — a beloved alpine restaurant with panoramic terrace views and refined Swiss-Italian cuisine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Acla da Fans or La Marmite (St. Moritz) — indulge in Engadine specialties such as Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup), venison, and house-made pasta paired with local Graubünden wines

day_by_day.notes: The Bernina Express from Poschiavo to St. Moritz is a UNESCO World Heritage railway journey — a spectacular experience in itself. Book first-class panoramic seats in advance. Alternatively, arrange a private chauffeured vehicle for maximum flexibility. Bobsled experience must be pre-booked; check availability for the Cresta Run (members/guests only) or the public Olympic Bob Run.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure by private luxury transfer to Zermatt (approximately 3–3.5 hours from Poschiavo via Chur or the scenic Glacier Express route). Arrive in Zermatt — a car-free alpine paradise beneath the iconic Matterhorn. Begin the Zermatt Ski Safari with a certified private ski guide. Access over 360km of world-class pistes across Switzerland and Italy, starting with the legendary Klein Matterhorn runs at 3,883m — the highest ski area in the Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Zermatt Ski Safari through the Rothorn and Sunnegga Paradise sectors. Enjoy off-piste powder runs with your guide if conditions allow. Take a scenic gondola to the Matterhorn Glacier Paradise for breathtaking 360-degree views of 38 Alpine peaks.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski at the iconic Vernissage Bar or Papperla Pub in Zermatt village. Enjoy a fondue or raclette dinner in a cozy mountain chalet restaurant before the private transfer back to Poschiavo.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the B&B before early departure — grab-and-go option with pastries, fruit, and thermos coffee arranged by the property
meals.lunch: On-mountain lunch at Chez Vrony (Findeln, Zermatt) — one of the most celebrated mountain restaurants in the Alps, with stunning Matterhorn views and refined Swiss cuisine including rösti, truffle dishes, and local wines
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Zum See (Zermatt) — a legendary alpine hut restaurant accessible by ski or snowcat, serving exquisite seasonal menus with game, truffles, and fine Swiss wines in a candlelit rustic setting

day_by_day.notes: Zermatt is car-free — arrange an electric taxi from Täsch (the last car-accessible village) into Zermatt. Ski equipment rental at the highest level (Stöckli, Völkl, or custom-fit) is available through premium rental shops in Zermatt. Book Chez Vrony and Zum See well in advance as they are extremely popular. Consider an overnight stay in Zermatt to avoid the long return transfer — luxury options include The Omnia or Mont Cervin Palace.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the B&B with a slow, indulgent breakfast. Take a gentle morning walk through the charming village of Poschiavo — a beautifully preserved Romansh-Italian border town with baroque architecture, the historic Piazza Comunale, and the Spanish Quarter. Visit the local market if available for artisan products.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart for the Glacier 3000 Suspension Bridge & Peak Walk experience (approximately 2.5 hours from Poschiavo via Aigle or Gstaad direction). Take the cable car up to Glacier 3000 (3,000m altitude) and walk across the Peak Walk by Tissot — the world's first suspension bridge connecting two mountain peaks. Enjoy panoramic views of Mont Blanc, the Matterhorn, and the Eiger. Optional: try the Alpine Coaster or snow bus on the glacier.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward Poschiavo or stop for dinner in the Gstaad or Château-d'Oex area — one of Switzerland's most exclusive alpine resort towns — before the scenic drive back.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely full breakfast at the B&B — Engadine specialties, bircher muesli, local jams, smoked salmon, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Peak Restaurant on Glacier 3000 — panoramic glass-enclosed dining with sweeping glacier views; enjoy Swiss classics like cheese soup, mountain charcuterie boards, and warm apple strudel
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Chesery (Gstaad) — a Michelin-starred institution offering refined French-Swiss cuisine in an elegant chalet setting, with an exceptional wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Glacier 3000 is located above Les Diablerets in the Vaud Alps — plan for a full-day excursion. The Peak Walk is weather-dependent; check conditions in advance. Dress in full thermal layers as temperatures at 3,000m can be extreme. The drive back to Poschiavo in the evening is scenic but long — consider hiring a private driver for the day for comfort and safety on mountain roads.

day_by_day.morning: Depart for the Jungfrau Region (approximately 2.5–3 hours from Poschiavo). Begin the Jungfrau Region Snowshoeing & Winter Hiking experience with a certified alpine guide. Trek through pristine snow-covered landscapes around Grindelwald or Mürren, with dramatic views of the Eiger North Face, Mönch, and Jungfrau. The guided tour takes you through untouched alpine terrain, frozen waterfalls, and silent winter forests.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Jungfraujoch cogwheel train — the 'Top of Europe' at 3,454m — for a once-in-a-lifetime alpine experience. Visit the Ice Palace carved inside the Aletsch Glacier, the Sphinx Observatory, and enjoy panoramic views across the longest glacier in the Alps. Optional: try the Snowpark or zip line at Jungfraujoch.
day_by_day.evening: Descend to Grindelwald or Interlaken for a celebratory dinner at one of the region's finest restaurants before the return transfer to Poschiavo.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the B&B before departure — hearty alpine spread with eggs, local meats, cheeses, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Crystal Restaurant at Jungfraujoch (Top of Europe) — a unique dining experience at 3,454m with panoramic glacier views and a curated Swiss menu
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Schmitte (Grindelwald) or Taverne (Interlaken) — elegant Swiss-Alpine cuisine featuring Bernese specialties such as Berner Platte, lake fish, and seasonal game, paired with Bernese wines

day_by_day.notes: Book Jungfraujoch tickets well in advance — this is one of Switzerland's most popular attractions and sells out quickly, especially in peak winter season. The snowshoeing tour should be arranged through a certified Jungfrau Region guide service. Altitude sickness can affect some visitors at Jungfraujoch — take time to acclimatize and stay hydrated. The return drive to Poschiavo is approximately 3 hours; a private driver is strongly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Immerse yourself in authentic Swiss mountain culture with the Traditional Swiss Alpine Cuisine & Cheese Cellar Tour. Visit a traditional alpine cheese dairy (Käserei) in the Graubünden region near Poschiavo or the Engadine Valley. Watch master cheesemakers craft Graubünden mountain cheese, taste aged varieties, and learn about centuries-old alpine dairy traditions. Follow with a guided visit to a local wine cellar featuring Graubünden Pinot Noir — one of Switzerland's finest wine regions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Poschiavo area for a relaxed afternoon. Explore the Val Poschiavo valley on a private guided snowshoe walk or a scenic horse-drawn sleigh ride through the snow-covered valley floor — a quintessentially Swiss alpine experience. Alternatively, enjoy a private spa session if available at the B&B or a nearby wellness facility.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Poschiavo or the nearby Engadine Valley — celebrate the penultimate evening of the trip with a special multi-course dinner featuring the finest local ingredients discovered throughout the week.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed breakfast at the B&B — enjoy the full spread one more time with local specialties and panoramic Bernina Pass views
meals.lunch: Lunch included as part of the Cheese Cellar Tour — a traditional alpine spread of freshly made cheese fondue, raclette, cured meats, pickles, and dark rye bread paired with local wines
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ristorante Suisse (Poschiavo) or a private chef dinner arranged at the B&B — a curated 5-course tasting menu featuring Graubünden specialties: Bündner Nusstorte, venison ragù, truffle polenta, and a selection of regional wines and digestifs

day_by_day.notes: The cheese cellar tour should be pre-arranged with a local agritourism operator in the Graubünden region. Horse-drawn sleigh rides in Val Poschiavo can be booked through local operators — a magical experience at dusk with the Bernina peaks glowing in alpenglow. Consider purchasing artisan cheese, local wines, and Bündner Nusstorte as premium gifts to take home.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the B&B with sweeping views of the Bernina Pass. Take a short, peaceful morning walk through Poschiavo village to soak in the last moments of alpine tranquility. Visit the historic Reformed Church of San Vittore or simply sit in the Piazza Comunale with a final espresso.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the B&B and depart by private luxury transfer to the airport (Zurich approximately 3 hours, Milan Malpensa approximately 2.5 hours). If time permits before departure, stop at a premium Swiss chocolate shop or delicatessen in Chur or along the route for last-minute luxury souvenirs — Läderach or Sprüngli chocolates, aged Graubünden cheese, and local Pinot Noir.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Switzerland. Reflect on an extraordinary week of world-class skiing, breathtaking alpine landscapes, gourmet Swiss cuisine, and unforgettable mountain experiences.

meals.breakfast: Final full alpine breakfast at the B&B — a celebratory spread with champagne or prosecco, fresh pastries, local cheeses, smoked meats, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Light lunch en route to the airport — stop at a premium restaurant in Chur such as Restaurant Stern or Zum Alten Zollhaus for refined regional cuisine and a farewell glass of Graubünden wine
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight premium dining (business/first class recommended for the return journey)

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for the transfer to the airport — mountain roads can be affected by winter weather conditions. Confirm your flight details and arrange private transfer pickup at least 4–5 hours before departure. Swiss customs allows generous allowances for food and wine purchases. Consider enrolling in a Swiss airport fast-track service for a seamless premium departure experience.
